Guides/Make it yours

Choose, import, and share themes

Pick a built-in look, bring colors over from VS Code or iTerm2, install community themes, and submit your own for review.

On this page

  • Pick a built-in theme
  • Import and export theme files
  • Browse and apply community themes
  • Submit a theme

Pick a built-in theme

  1. Open Settings > Appearance. The Skin menu lists the 22 built-in themes under Follow System, Light Themes, and Dark Themes.
  2. Choose a skin. Pathem shows it on the window right away and opens Theme Preview. Choose Apply to keep it or Cancel to return to the look you had.
  3. Adjust single values if you want to. Accent color and Window tint change the two theme colors, and None clears the window tint. Appearance switches between System, Light, and Dark.
  4. Each theme also brings a folder style, a file icon set, and toolbar glyphs. Use the Folder style, File icons, and Toolbar glyphs menus to override any of them. Choose Use Theme in a menu to go back to what the theme supplies.
  5. Choose Reset Theme to return to the System appearance and colors.
Keep in mind

A skin tints Pathem's own selection, panes, tabs, and breadcrumb. Standard buttons keep the macOS accent color. The style menus keep an explicit choice when you change skins, so set them to Use Theme to see a theme exactly as it was designed. The embedded terminal has its own Theme setting.

Import and export theme files

  1. In Settings > Appearance, choose Import… and select a file. The same button accepts a Pathem theme file (.json), a VS Code color theme (.json or .jsonc), and an iTerm2 color preset (.itermcolors).
  2. Check Theme Preview. It names what will change and shows a color swatch. Choose Apply to save it or Cancel to leave everything as it was.
  3. To save your current look, choose Export… and pick a location. The file is named Pathem Theme.json unless you rename it, and it records your colors, appearance, and the folder, file icon, and toolbar styles in effect, including any overrides.
  • A Pathem theme file can carry colors, styles, and its own small icon artwork. Older files that hold only colors keep your current styles.
  • A VS Code theme supplies the window background and the accent color, and its light or dark type sets the appearance. Pathem reads the editor or sidebar background and the focus, badge, or button color. Translucent colors are skipped, and your current styles stay as they are.
  • An iTerm2 preset changes the embedded terminal only: foreground, background, cursor, and the 16 ANSI colors. Colors the preset leaves out keep their current values. Shell and font settings are not read.
  • Import files can be up to 512 KB. A file that is too large or not a recognized theme is rejected before anything changes.

Browse and apply community themes

To look through the published themes in a browser first, with screenshots, colors, and licenses, see the community themes gallery.

  1. In Settings > Appearance, click Themes… to open the gallery. Pathem downloads the current public catalog and opens the Themes window.
  2. Stay on Browse and use the search field to filter by title, creator, or tag. Select a listing to see its creator credit, license, version, and screenshots.
  3. Choose Preview to try the theme on your window. Choose Close Preview to restore your appearance.
  4. Choose Install to keep a copy on your Mac, then Apply Installed to switch to it. When a newer revision is published, the listing offers Update.
  5. Open Installed to see the themes you have. Apply switches to one, and Uninstall… removes it. If the theme you uninstall is the one applied, Pathem returns to the System appearance.
Keep in mind

Opening the Themes window is the only time Pathem contacts the catalog. The request is an ordinary download of a public file. It does not include your files, file names, installed themes, or search text, and searching happens on your Mac. If you never open the window, nothing is fetched. A theme that is later withdrawn from the catalog stays installed until you uninstall it.

Submit a theme

Everything in the issue is public: the theme, its title and summary, your creator credit, license, source, tags, the screenshots, and your GitHub account name. Pathem itself uploads nothing. The file becomes public only when you attach it to the issue.

Pathem re-encodes each screenshot before it goes into the file. Camera and location metadata is removed, and the image is scaled down as needed so each published preview fits within 300 KB.

A maintainer reviews every submission by hand. Approved themes are added to the public catalog and appear the next time someone opens the Themes window. A reviewer may ask for changes on the issue, and a listing can be withdrawn later.

  1. Set up the look you want to share in Settings > Appearance, then choose Submit a Theme…. The submission captures the theme as it is at that moment.
  2. Choose one to three PNG or JPEG screenshots, each up to 2 MB and 2400 pixels per side. Pick images you are willing to publish, and check that no private file names or paths are visible in them.
  3. Fill in Prepare Marketplace Submission: Listing ID, Revision, Title, Summary, Creator credit, and License, plus the optional Source and Tags. The listing ID is lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, for example tidal-marsh.
  4. Choose Save and Continue… and save the file. It is named after the listing ID and revision and ends in .submission.json. Nothing has been sent anywhere yet.
  5. In Submission Ready, choose Open GitHub Form, or choose Done for Now and open the form later from the Pathem repository's New Issue page.
  6. Sign in with your GitHub account and complete the Submit a Pathem theme form: Theme name and listing ID, Revision, Submission JSON (drag the saved file into this field), License, About this revision, and the Permission to share checkbox. Then submit the issue.
  7. To update a theme or respond to review, prepare a new file with the same listing ID and a higher revision, and submit it the same way.
